sourceEvidence.quote:
Agents that block lymphocyte activation and proliferation. Reduce acute transplant rejection by
suppressing cellular immunity (used as prophylaxis). Frequently combined to achieve greater
efficacy with ↓ toxicity. Chronic suppression ↑ risk of infection and malignancy.

kypExtensions.summary: The target map read as four blockade levels (receptor [basiliximab], transcription [calcineurin inhibitors], response [sirolimus/mTOR], proliferation [antimetabolites]) plus the global glucocorticoid/NF-κB layer — with the combination logic (cross-level pairing for efficacy with less toxicity), the FKBP-synergy explanation, and the interaction/withdrawal bridges (allopurinol dosing rules, HPA-axis taper, demargination leukocytosis).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source lists drugs without the cascade-level organization or the combination rationale; these integrations are KYP's design. Allopurinol dose-reduction specifics and stress-dosing protocols are labeled extension.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + mechanism caption + callout + patterns + mnemonics + miniCase

notes: Census: p140 carries only 1x1 artifacts + one decorative index strip (page furniture) — the T-helper-cell signaling diagram is pure vector; p141's rasters belong to the cytokines section owned by E41. One original KYP registry visual (immunosuppressant-target-map) redraws the signaling diagram as the four-level blockade map with the printed rules panel and the seven-drug roster. MNEMONIC BOUNDARY (E22+ rule, table-block precedent): FA's printed mnemonics ('Sir Basil's kidney transplant', 'Kidney sir-vives', 'Pansirtopenia' [also the verbatim toxicity text], 'azathiopurine') are quoted in manifest evidence for verification and carried verbatim where they ARE the source's table text, but are NOT reproduced in the registry visual; KYP originals replace them in the mnemonics field. Quoting note: the drug tables' columns interleave — quotes follow the physical line order. Boundary: the Recombant cytokines table on p141's lower half is owned by E41 (heading pinned here as boundary evidence).
